description: ​Hi! We are working on the "Flame in Freefall" challenge. Our goal is to build an intelligent RAG/LLM platform to analyze NASA's microgravity combustion experiments. We bring strong Python, FastAPI, and data engineering skills. Looking for motivated teammates (Frontend, UI/UX, or Data/Domain experts) to build a winning project together!
summary:
PyroLens is a Scientific Evidence Intelligence platform built for the "Flame in Freefall" challenge to transform fragmented NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion data into traceable engineering evidence for spacecraft fire safety.

Instead of acting as a generic PDF chatbot, PyroLens ingests 24 NASA PSI combustion investigations (including BASS, BASS-II, Saffire-I–III, FLEX, ACME, and SAME), parses 20 experimental CSV tables cell by cell (13,668 measurements across 1,330 eligible observations), and normalizes heterogeneous units (mole fraction vs. % O₂, psi/mmHg/atm vs. kPa) while deriving oxygen partial pressure (pO₂).

Engineers can define mission scenarios—such as a Lunar Surface Habitat (34% O₂, 8.2 psi, 0.165 g, concurrent airflow)—to run physical-condition matching, inspect 2D Research Gap Intelligence heatmaps (O₂ × pressure), trace every claim back to exact source cells (e.g., PSI-99:r5:c6) and DOIs, and export Markdown, CSV, or JSON evidence reports.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

PyroLens turns raw, heterogeneous NASA combustion research into structured, auditable engineering evidence. The backend ingests 24 NASA PSI Combustion Science investigations, 20 published experimental tables (13,668 cell measurements, 1,330 combustion observations), 352 linked publications, and NASA reference documents such as "A Researcher's Guide to Combustion Science."

Core Capabilities:

1. Unit Normalization & Scenario Builder: Engineers specify target mission parameters (oxygen concentration, total pressure, flow velocity, flow configuration—concurrent vs. opposed, specimen geometry, diluent gas, and gravity environment). PyroLens explicitly converts units (e.g., 8.2 psi → 56.54 kPa, % O₂ ↔ mole fraction) and computes derived oxygen partial pressure (pO₂) while preserving original values and conversion provenance.

2. Physical-Condition Matching Engine: Compares target mission envelopes against real PSI experiment rows (e.g., Saffire-I/II/III, BASS/BASS-II, FLEX/FLEX-2, ACME, SAME/SAME-R), classifying each parameter as match, partial, mismatch, or not reported with exact cell citations (e.g., PSI-99:r5:c6).

3. Research Gap Intelligence: Generates multidimensional coverage matrices (such as Oxygen Mole Fraction × Total Pressure) over real experimental rows, explicitly identifying unstudied exploration regimes (e.g., 32.5–35% O₂ at 50–65 kPa for lunar habitats) and explaining exclusions (e.g., diluent mismatches).

4. Traceable Scientific Output & Anti-Hallucination: Every record links to an Experiment Passport, DOI, and source cell. The optional SI/LLM assistant separates claims into EVIDENCE, INTERPRETATION, HYPOTHESIS, and SAFETY, verifying EVIDENCE claims against cited excerpts and downgrading unsupported statements. Engineers can export rule-based Markdown, CSV, and JSON evidence reports.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Spacecraft, lunar habitats, and pressurized rovers operate under elevated oxygen (~30–34% O₂) and reduced pressure (≤8.2–10.2 psi), where buoyancy-free or partial-gravity flames behave differently from 1-g terrestrial tests. PyroLens saves fire-safety engineers hours of manual table reconciliation and prevents false confidence by exposing both what NASA PSI data proves and where experimental coverage is missing.

Technology Stack

- Backend: Python 3, FastAPI, Pydantic 2, Uvicorn, httpx, in-process BM25 retrieval, deterministic unit-normalization and cell-provenance pipeline.

- Frontend: React 18, TypeScript (strict), Vite 5, Tailwind CSS 3, Recharts, custom SVG Evidence Graph and coverage heatmaps.

- Optional SI/LLM Layer: OpenAI / Anthropic API integration with lexical citation verification (also runs fully offline in deterministic rule-based mode).

Creativity & Engineering Considerations

Our team prioritized epistemic honesty over flashy AI claims: PyroLens never fabricates missing measurements, never silently converts incompatible units, clearly separates conceptual visualizations from experimental NASA imagery, and explicitly labels demonstration assumptions versus verified PSI observations.

Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure

SI/LLM tools were used strictly as an optional synthesis layer inside the assistant (with automated citation verification against retrieved PSI/document excerpts) and to assist with code development and conceptual 1-g vs. µg flame visualization in the demonstration video (labeled on-screen as "Conceptual visualization — not experimental imagery or NASA data"). All numerical data, unit conversions, gap matrices, and evidence reports are computed deterministically without generative AI.
